materials.title: A call about the dance class
materials.text:
Woman: Park Hall Dance School. Good afternoon.
Ruby: Hello. Is there a class for children who have never danced before?
Woman: Yes, on Wednesday. It begins at four fifteen and ends at five.
Ruby: I am ten. Can I come?
Woman: The group is for children from nine to twelve. Your parent should book before Tuesday evening.
Ruby: Do I need special shoes for the first lesson?
Woman: No. Clean indoor shoes are fine. Wear clothes you can move in easily.
Ruby: Can my brother wait for me inside?
Woman: He can sit in the waiting room with an adult. Children must not wait alone in the car park.
Ruby: How much does the first class cost?
Woman: Five pounds. Bring a water bottle; there is a place to fill it.
Ruby: Thank you. Mum will call to book.
Woman: Please tell her about the Wednesday time and Tuesday booking deadline.

questions.prompt: When does the class start?
questions.explanation: Class starts16:15 Wednesday.17:00 is finish and Tuesday evening the booking deadline.

questions.prompt: Can ten-year-old Ruby join?
questions.explanation: Ten is within9–12. The other age rules contradict it.

questions.prompt: What shoes are suitable for the first lesson?
questions.explanation: Special shoes are not needed; clean indoor shoes are fine. Wet boots are not the stated suitable type.

questions.prompt: Where can Ruby’s brother wait?
options: On the dance floor during class
In the waiting room with an adult
questions.explanation: Waiting room plus adult is permitted. Alone in car park is prohibited and dance-floor waiting not offered.

questions.prompt: What should Ruby bring?
questions.explanation: A refillable bottle is requested. Group meal/chair are not requirements.

materials.title: Booking a small party room
materials.text:
Man: Town Centre Rooms. Can I help?
Ben: Hello. Our family wants a room for my sister's birthday on Sunday.
Man: We have the Blue Room from two to five. It holds twelve people.
Ben: There will be ten of us. Can we bring a cake?
Man: Yes. You may bring cold food and drinks, but no cooking is allowed in the room.
Ben: Are there plates and cups?
Man: We provide tables and chairs only. Bring your own plates and cups.
Ben: Can we arrive at one thirty to decorate?
Man: Yes, but the room will not be ready before then. Everything must be cleared away by five thirty.
Ben: How much is the room?
Man: Thirty pounds, including the half-hour before and after. An adult must make the booking.
Ben: Thank you. I will tell Dad about the times and what we need to bring.

questions.prompt: How many people can the Blue Room hold?
questions.explanation: Capacity is12. Ten is their group size and30 the cost.

questions.prompt: What food arrangement is allowed?
options: Bringing a cake and cold food
Cooking a hot meal in the room
questions.explanation: Cold food/cake are allowed; cooking is not and no kitchen is provided.

questions.prompt: Which items must the family bring?
questions.explanation: Only tables/chairs supplied, so plates/cups come from visitors. Door is not a party item.

questions.prompt: When may decorating begin?
questions.explanation: Earliest entry is13:30. Earlier is not ready,17:30 is cleanup deadline.

questions.prompt: Who must book the room?
questions.explanation: An adult makes the booking. The children are not authorized to book alone.

materials.title: Crab and the straight line
materials.text:
In this story, Crab and Rabbit draw a line in the sand for a game. They want to roll a small ball from one end to the other without crossing the line.

Rabbit rolls first. His ball moves quickly, then turns and crosses the line. He says the sand must be unfair. Crab looks at the ground. A little stone sits in the ball's path.

They move to a clear patch and draw the line again. Rabbit rolls too hard, and the ball goes far beyond the end. Crab tries a gentle push. His ball stops halfway.

For the next turn, neither animal asks who is best. They change one thing at a time: where they start and how strongly they push. Soon both can stop close to the end.

Then the tide reaches their lines. The water washes the game away. Rabbit looks disappointed, but Crab puts the ball in a bucket. "We still have this," he says. "We can draw another line tomorrow."

The next morning, Rabbit arrives with two balls. One is much larger. Crab laughs. "Now we have a new question before we begin."

questions.prompt: What do Crab and Rabbit first try to do?
options: Roll a ball along a line
questions.explanation: They roll along the line. Sandcastles/fishing are not the game.

questions.prompt: What changes the first ball’s direction?
options: A rabbit hiding in the sea
A small stone in its path
questions.explanation: Crab spots the stone in the path. Sea rabbit/bucket hole are not stated.

questions.prompt: What happens when Rabbit rolls too hard?
options: The ball passes the far end
questions.explanation: His hard push goes beyond the end. Halfway is Crab’s gentle attempt; tree is impossible here.

questions.prompt: What removes the lines?
questions.explanation: Water washes them away. No cleaner/tool appears.

questions.prompt: Why is there a new question the next day?
options: The two balls are different sizes
questions.explanation: The larger second ball changes the comparison. Balls remain and Rabbit comes to play.

materials.title: Owl’s quiet part
materials.text:
In this fictional story, the forest animals prepare a play. Fox wants to be the traveller because that character speaks often. Mouse chooses a shopkeeper with a funny song. Owl is given the part of the night wind.

Owl is unhappy. The wind has only three lines, and nobody will see her behind the painted trees. She asks Rabbit, the director, for a bigger part.

Rabbit suggests trying one rehearsal first. When Owl says her first line in a loud, cheerful voice, Fox laughs. The traveller is supposed to feel alone in the dark. Owl tries again, speaking slowly and softly. This time Fox stops smiling and looks around as though the forest has changed.

At the performance, Owl waits quietly for each cue. She cannot see much of the audience, but she can hear their sudden silence when the wind begins.

Afterwards, Mouse says the night scene was her favourite. Owl still likes speaking more than three lines in ordinary conversation. For this play, however, the quiet part has given her something interesting to do. She keeps a tiny painted tree from the set beside her programme.

questions.prompt: Which part does Owl first receive?
questions.explanation: Owl is wind; Fox traveller and Mouse shopkeeper.

questions.prompt: Why is Owl unhappy at first?
options: She must sing every song alone
She has few lines and is hidden
She has lost the entire script
questions.explanation: Only three unseen lines concern her. Script loss/all-songs duty are not stated.

questions.prompt: What does Rabbit suggest?
questions.explanation: Rabbit asks for one trial. Cancellation/one-actor plan are not proposed.

questions.prompt: What changes when Owl speaks softly?
options: The traveller’s lonely night feels more convincing
The painted trees turn into real ones
questions.explanation: Fox reacts as though the atmosphere changed. The set remains painted and he does not leave.

questions.prompt: What does Owl keep afterwards?
questions.explanation: She keeps a tiny set tree with programme. Chairs/shop are not her memento.

materials.title: Four library reading groups
materials.text:
The library offers four reading groups this month. Each meeting is for one age group, and booking is required. The price is for one meeting and includes the reading material.

| Group | When | Age | Price | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Story Builders | Tuesday 16:00–17:00 | 8–10 | £3 | Read a short story and create another ending. |
| Nature Pages | Wednesday 16:30–17:30 | 10–12 | £4 | Read about wildlife and discuss a photograph. |
| Comic Corner | Saturday 10:00–11:15 | 9–12 | £5 | Compare pictures and speech bubbles in a comic. |
| Family Tales | Sunday 14:00–15:00 | All ages | £2 | Each child comes with an adult; both need a ticket. |

Children should arrive ten minutes early. Pens and paper are provided. Family Tales allows children under eight; the other groups follow their listed ages. Meetings are indoors. Booking closes the day before each session, if places remain. The café sells snacks separately, and food should stay outside the reading rooms. A cancelled library meeting is refunded; visitors who cannot attend should contact the desk as early as possible.

questions.prompt: Which group can a seven-year-old attend?
questions.explanation: Only Family Tales allows under-eight children, with adult attendance. Other groups exclude age7.

questions.prompt: When should Comic Corner participants arrive?
questions.explanation: Ten minutes before10:00 Saturday is9:50. The others are late/wrong day.

questions.prompt: How much do one adult and one child pay for Family Tales?
questions.explanation: Each needs a£2 ticket, so total£4. Two is one person and six not the two-ticket price.

questions.prompt: Which group discusses a wildlife photograph?
questions.explanation: Nature Pages explicitly combines wildlife reading/photo discussion.

questions.prompt: What is included in the meeting price?
questions.explanation: Materials included; snacks separate and travel not included.

materials.title: Four try-it sessions
materials.text:
The youth centre has four beginner sessions. You may book one or more if the times do not overlap. Prices are per person. Each session provides basic equipment and a teacher.

| Session | Day and time | Minimum age | Price | Bring |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Paper Buildings | Monday 10:00–11:30 | 8 | £4 | A box to carry the model home. |
| Rhythm Games | Monday 13:00–14:00 | 7 | £3 | A water bottle. |
| Nature Sketching | Tuesday 10:00–12:00 | 10 | £6 | A hat and suitable outdoor shoes. |
| Shadow Theatre | Tuesday 14:00–15:30 | 9 | £5 | A short story idea; writing it out is optional. |

Arrive fifteen minutes early to register. Paper Buildings, Rhythm Games and Shadow Theatre are indoors. Nature Sketching moves to the covered courtyard if light rain is expected; the teacher may cancel in unsuitable conditions. Please tell the centre about access requirements before booking so the activity can be discussed. Children are collected by the named adult at the end. The centre does not provide lunch or supervision between separate sessions, so families must make their own arrangement for the gap.

questions.prompt: Which session can an eight-year-old join?
questions.explanation: Paper Buildings minimum8 includes age8. Nature minimum10, shadows9 exclude it.

questions.prompt: When should Rhythm Games participants arrive?
questions.explanation: Fifteen minutes before13:00 Monday is12:45. Other times are late or different session/day.

questions.prompt: What is needed for Paper Buildings?
options: A box for taking the model home
A hat for a long outdoor walk
questions.explanation: The Bring column specifies a carrying box. Basic equipment provided; hat is nature-sketch requirement.

questions.prompt: What happens to Nature Sketching in light rain?
options: It always moves to Monday morning
It may use the covered courtyard
questions.explanation: The covered courtyard is the light-rain arrangement. Day change/swimming are not offered.

questions.prompt: What must a family arrange between morning and afternoon sessions?
questions.explanation: No lunch or gap supervision provided. Overnight stay is not part of day sessions.
